newsitem.title: USA: Gold prices hits two-month low, crude oil falls.
newsitem.headline: Gold prices hits two-month low, crude oil falls.

text.p: Gold prices fell to a two-month low Monday, partly on news that the International Monetary Fund this week may approve the sale of five million ounces of IMF gold.
Crude oil and gasoline prices closed lower amid easing tensions in Iraq, while wheat prices rose on bullish export news.
The Commodity Research Bureau index of 17 commodities fell 0.16 point to 247.79.
The IMF sale has been overhanging the gold market for many weeks, but the plan may be approved this week.

"Gold bullion slipped below $385.00 (per ounce) in London and there was renewed concern about the IMF gold sales plan being approved at the IMF board meeting this week, even though that is an old story," said a New York trader.
The IMF plan calls for the sale of about five million ounces of the IMF's 103.5 million ounce reserve to help finance a proposed programme to alleviate debt in developing countries.
With inflation apparently under control, investor demand for gold also slackened.

"Fabricator demand for precious metals has remained weak even though summer is nearly over and investor demand remains weak especially from the Far East," Credit Suisse New York vice president Ian MacDonald said.
Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the Council of Economic Advisors, said Monday he currently sees no evidence of inflationary pressures on the U.S. economy.
"Wages have been at a level...that does not represent an inflationary threat," he said.
At New York's Commodity Exchange, gold for December delivery closed $1.60 lower at $387.20 per ounce.

Crude oil prices fell at the New York Mercantile Exchange after soaring last week to the highest levels since the Gulf War. There has been no additional military action against Iraq since the United States last week launched cruise missiles into the Arab country.

Iraq's attack on Kurd residents in the north not only prompted the cruise missle attack, but led to the suspension of a United Nations-sponsored oil-for-food deal. Under the deal, Iraq would have been allowed to sell oil for six months to pay for food and medicine.
NYMEX crude oil for October delivery was down $0.12 at $23.73 a barrel.
The drop in crude oil plus a seasonal slowdown in gasoline use took NYMEX gasoline futures lower in light trading.
"Gasoline is just being neglected. The season is over," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt, citing the end of summer, which is the period of peak demand for gasoline.
NYMEX October gasoline was down 1.18 cents at 64.09 cents per gallon.
Wheat futures closed higher at the Chicago Board of Trade after U.S. government figures showed an unexpected surge in export demand last week.
"The wheat export number was higher than expected and that popped wheat," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

The Agriculture Department on Monday said 33.588 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended Sept. 5. That was well above the 26.586 million the previous week and above trader expectations, which ranged from 22 million to 26 million bushels.
News Egypt bought 100,000 metric tons of U.S. wheat also was supportive.

CBOT soft red winter wheat for December delivery closed up 6-1/4 cents at $4.48 per bushel. At the Kansas City Board of Trade, hard red winter wheat for December closed up 1-1/2 cents at $4.47, and Minneapolis Grain Exchange December spring wheat rose 1-1/2 to $4.30-3/4.
